vision.one_line: Evidence-backed international caller-campaign intelligence that people and agents can inspect, act on, and privately monitor.
vision.north_star: Any person or agent can turn an unfamiliar displayed phone number into a country-aware, source-backed caller-campaign answer, take a concrete safety action, and privately monitor material changes.
vision.promise: Normalize once, check eligible country-aware evidence, explain the calibrated campaign risk and uncertainty, and offer a safe next action without guessing identity or safety.
vision.wedge: One shared lookup and caller-campaign contract across CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web, starting with official NL, GB, and US evidence and expanding through controlled first-party reports, private watches, verified organisation declarations, corpus transparency, and hosted MCP.
target_users: Agents deciding how to handle an unfamiliar phone number
Developers integrating caller context into safety-conscious products
Maintainers adding lawful, source-backed country coverage
People who want a private alert when a watched number's risk context materially changes
Organisations declaring official contact routes without claiming call origin

principles.title: Agent-first product surface
principles.rule: Versioned structured output is canonical; prose, CLI tables, and web pages render the same result.
good: MCP structuredContent and CLI JSON validate against one schema
bad: A web-only conclusion that cannot be reproduced by an agent

principles.title: JSON-first durable contracts
principles.rule: Canonical product contracts, workflow state, evidence events, and acceptance records are machine-readable JSON or JSONL; Markdown explains rather than replaces them.
good: A fresh agent can validate and route work without extracting state from prose
bad: A critical safety rule exists only inside a narrative planning page

principles.title: Displayed number is not caller identity
principles.rule: Describe evidence about a call displaying a number; never present that display value as proof of the caller or subscriber.
good: Reports say that a call displayed the number and explain spoofing risk
bad: The owner of this number is a scammer

principles.title: Keep evidence classes separate
principles.rule: Lookup demand, number-plan facts, allocation evidence, identity claims, and call reports remain distinct records.
good: Search activity is an aggregate demand metric only
bad: High lookup volume increases a fraud score

principles.title: Evidence before verdict
principles.rule: Every assessment exposes sources, retrieval time, confidence, reason codes, gaps, and residual uncertainty.
good: Unknown is returned when evidence cannot support a stronger label
bad: A proprietary AI score with no inspectable evidence

principles.title: Country-aware number interpretation
principles.rule: Canonicalize to E.164 while retaining raw input, origin region, national display, and parsing decisions.
good: National input without a country code requires an explicit origin region
bad: Guessing a country from deployment location or interface language

principles.title: Fail closed and visibly
principles.rule: Unavailable, stale, contradictory, or unsupported evidence becomes a typed gap rather than an inferred identity or safety claim.
good: One failed country source leaves a source-specific gap in the result
bad: A source timeout silently becomes no reports and therefore safe

principles.title: Public-safe by default
principles.rule: Fixtures, documentation, logs, screenshots, and repository history exclude real personal numbers, secrets, and private reports.
good: Documentation uses officially reserved fictional numbers
bad: A real missed-call number is committed as a convenient test fixture

principles.title: Sustainable source use
principles.rule: Every country adapter declares source authority, reuse basis, permitted fields, retrieval time, and portability limitations.
good: Official datasets are pinned or fetched under documented reuse terms
bad: Unlicensed competitor pages are copied into a permanent database

principles.title: Make uncertainty readable
principles.rule: Interfaces lead with normalized context and evidence, then state confidence and unknowns in plain language without alarmist decoration.
good: Unknown, unverified, and verified states remain distinguishable without color alone
bad: A red warning implies fraud when the only fact is a new lookup

principles.title: Compact, not shallow
principles.rule: Default results stay concise while preserving stable handles for sources, gaps, evidence, and methodology.
good: An agent can answer quickly and retrieve deeper evidence by identifier
bad: Verbose prose hides missing provenance or contradictory observations

principles.title: Four calibrated risk states
principles.rule: Every surface leads with exactly one of official_warning, elevated_signals, no_risk_evidence, or insufficient_evidence and pairs it with an explicit next action.
good: No risk evidence requires a current eligible risk-capable source and explicitly states that it does not mean safe
bad: A source-confidence percentage is styled like a probability that answering is safe

principles.title: Rights before ingestion
principles.rule: Only official, explicitly licensed, or first-party moderated evidence may enter reputation processing after a machine-readable source and privacy gate passes.
good: A disabled source record carries zero permitted fields until written permission is documented
bad: Robots permission or public visibility is treated as a licence to republish reports

principles.title: Campaigns carry durable risk context
principles.rule: A caller campaign groups eligible observations about calls displaying bounded values over time; it never asserts the identity behind a call.
good: A corrected campaign retains its dates, evidence handles, status, and spoofing limitation
bad: A phone-number owner is labelled as the actor behind every matching call

principles.title: Monitoring is private and sparse
principles.rule: A watch requires verified consent, stores minimized contact material, stays non-public, and notifies only on material state changes.
good: A subscriber can list, revoke, expire, correct, and delete a watch without exposing it publicly
bad: A public lookup reveals who is watching a number or every search triggers a message

principles.title: Verified declaration is not call origin
principles.rule: Organisation verification proves only that an organisation declared a bounded official contact route; caller ID can still be spoofed.
good: The interface labels an official contact route and repeats that a displayed call may be spoofed
bad: A verified portfolio badge guarantees that a matching call came from the organisation

non_goals: Expose or infer private subscriber identities from contacts, breaches, or scraped profiles.
Track the physical location of a caller or claim that numbering geography is live location.
Treat number validity, range allocation, or an original carrier as proof of current assignment.
Let lookup volume, virality, or a single report create a fraud verdict.
Describe no matching risk evidence as proof that answering or returning a call is safe.
Republish proprietary third-party reputation data without a permitted integration.
Build outbound calling, call recording, contact enrichment, or surveillance features.
assumptions: Official numbering-allocation evidence is lawfully reusable for the initial three-country wedge.
Users can supply an origin region when a number lacks an international country code.
Agents and developers prefer calibrated uncertainty over an unsupported identity guess.
A prominent four-state result can improve decision clarity without collapsing uncertainty into a binary safe or dangerous label.
Third-party caller-report data remains unavailable unless explicit permission or a compatible licence is recorded.
Source-specific adapters can remain independent while sharing one evidence contract.
Phone-number portability and spoofing will remain material limitations.

forbidden: Secrets, access tokens, credentials, or private configuration
Real personal phone numbers in fixtures, screenshots, or documentation
Private subscriber identity sourced from contacts, breaches, or scraped profiles
Unlicensed third-party datasets or copied proprietary reports
Guilt, fraud, or safety conclusions derived from popularity alone
Raw requester IP addresses or personal lookup histories in product analytics
required_boundaries: State that caller ID can be spoofed and describes a displayed number
Distinguish allocation holder from current provider and subscriber
Return no risk evidence only after a current eligible risk-capable source is checked, and never treat it as proof of safety
Keep lookup activity separate from reputation inputs
Allow only official, explicitly licensed, or first-party moderated evidence to influence risk states
Attach source, retrieval time, confidence, and reason codes to assessments
Support correction, objection, deletion, moderation, and source takedown
Aggregate public search activity only above an anti-enumeration threshold
public_safety.privacy_posture: Minimize collection, avoid raw personal lookup histories, keep real runtime data out of Git, document purpose and retention, and require an approved legal and privacy basis before accepting public reports or imported reputation data.
public_safety.moderation_posture: Community reports remain unverified observations until independent evidence, abuse controls, and correction processes support a stronger state.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Do machine-facing artifacts validate against committed schemas?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: The local contract suite parses and validates every canonical JSON artifact.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Do CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web surfaces render one shared result?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Contract fixtures pass unchanged through every implemented adapter.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Is local-number interpretation explicit and reproducible?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: National input records an origin region; ambiguous input fails with typed guidance.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can a reviewer trace every conclusion to evidence?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Assessments expose source identifiers, retrieval times, reasons, gaps, and confidence.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does public wording avoid equating caller ID with caller identity?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Schemas, fixtures, interfaces, and moderation language use displayed-number semantics.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Are demand, facts, claims, reports, and assessments independent?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Storage and aggregation tests prevent cross-class mutation and popularity scoring.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can privacy and correction obligations be executed?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Retention, correction, deletion, objection, and incident paths have tested runbooks.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can a new developer or agent continue from a clean clone?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: One documented command validates contracts, docs, workflow state, and public safety.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does adding a country preserve evidence quality?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Each adapter passes the same provenance, rights, freshness, and failure conformance suite.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Is the prominent risk state useful without implying unsupported safety or guilt?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Every surface renders one shared four-state result, an explicit next action, and residual spoofing uncertainty without presenting source confidence as safety probability.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can every reputation input prove that it is eligible for ingestion?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Every enabled source has machine-validated authority, reuse basis, permitted fields, privacy status, freshness, outage behavior, and takedown ownership.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can each public caller campaign be inspected, corrected, and understood without an identity claim?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Every campaign exposes bounded membership, dates, eligible evidence, diversity, confidence, freshness, actions, correction state, and a spoofing limitation.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can a person monitor material changes without creating a public or enumerable subscriber trail?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Watch tests prove ownership verification, minimization, private listing, idempotent material-change delivery, expiry, revocation, correction, and deletion.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does organisation verification remain narrower than caller-origin proof?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Challenge, expiry, replay, conflict, audit, correction, deletion, appeal, and public spoofing-language tests all pass.

review_checklist: Confirm every public phone number is officially reserved or structurally redacted.
Confirm caller, subscriber, provider, and range-holder language is not conflated.
Confirm unavailable evidence produces an explicit gap rather than a safe result.
Confirm lookup activity cannot change reputation or moderation outcomes.
Confirm new sources document authority, reuse basis, freshness, and permitted fields.
Confirm every assessment includes provenance, reason codes, confidence, and residual risk.
Confirm logs and metrics avoid raw phone numbers, requester identities, and lookup trails.
Confirm schemas, fixtures, tests, documentation, and interfaces stay version-aligned.
Confirm public copy remains calm, accessible, specific, and non-accusatory.
Confirm official_warning, elevated_signals, no_risk_evidence, and insufficient_evidence remain textually and visually distinct.
Confirm source confidence is subordinate to the risk state and is never presented as a safety percentage.
Confirm campaign membership describes calls displaying bounded values and never subscriber or caller identity.
Confirm watches are private, verified, revocable, minimized, and triggered only by material changes.
Confirm verified organisation portfolios are presented as declarations rather than proof of call origin.
Confirm a fresh clone passes the documented local gate without private dependencies.

maturity_model.meaning: Repository identity, workflow, vision, safety, public documentation, and validation contracts are complete.
maturity_model.exit_evidence: Public repository gates pass and the product backlog is dependency-ordered.

maturity_model.meaning: NL, GB, and US official evidence can be queried through one shared read-only result contract with a calibrated four-state risk presentation.
maturity_model.exit_evidence: CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web risk-state parity plus country-adapter conformance and visual proof pass.

maturity_model.meaning: Eligible evidence and explicit first-party observations can form explainable caller campaigns under source-rights, privacy, abuse, correction, and durable-data controls.
maturity_model.exit_evidence: Campaign, source-rights, moderation, retention, deletion, objection, appeal, anti-brigading, and storage gates pass.

maturity_model.meaning: Private watches, verified organisation declarations, public corpus transparency, and hosted MCP make campaign intelligence useful between one-off searches.
maturity_model.exit_evidence: Consent, anti-enumeration, notification, verification, transparency, remote-protocol, and live-deployment gates pass.

residual_risk_wording: A phone-number lookup can describe numbering context and reported activity, but caller ID may be spoofed and the evidence does not prove who placed a call.
